newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Brittan to seek clarification on US telecom offer.
newsitem.headline: Brittan to seek clarification on US telecom offer.

text.p: EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan will seek details from acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on the "wide-ranging" U.S. exemption on satellite transmission services, a EU official said.

The U.S. exemption to most-favoured-nation treatment for direct-to-home broadcast and direct broadcast satellite television services as well as digital audiovisual services was presented at telecom talks at the World Trade Organisation.
Canada said it was also seeking clarification from the U.S. on the U.S. exemption, seen by some diplomats as violating the services agreement under the Uruguay Round.
"We are seeking clarity. So far the U.S. has declined to
explain," a EU official told reporters.
"This is being presented to us as a fait accompli. It is a unilateral declaration," he added.
The EU official called the U.S. exemption "wide-ranging," adding: "It is much wider than anything anyone else has done.
"We hope there will be contacts between Sir Leon and Mrs.
Barshefsky later on. We've requested an opportunity to discuss this. We had no prediction from them that they were taking anything off the table."
Brittan was to chair a EU General Affairs Council, comprised of ministers from the 13 member states, in Geneva late on Friday. "We have to provisionally assess the situation."

Trade officials quoted U.S. Deputy Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang as telling the WTO meeting that he hoped a "critical mass" of offers would be on the table by Saturday in time for an accord to be clinched.
Lang called the U.S. addition a "narrow MFN exemption."
